title: Cyclic orderings of matroids
exact_target:
If a matroid's ground set splits into bases, can all its elements
be cyclically arranged so that every rank-sized consecutive block is a basis?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
A finite matroid $M=(S,\mathcal I)$ consists of a family of independent
subsets containing $\varnothing$, closed under subsets, and satisfying
exchange: if $I,J\in\mathcal I$ and $|I|<|J|$, some $e\in J\setminus I$
has $I\cup\{e\}\in\mathcal I$. Its bases are the maximal independent
sets; all have the same cardinality $r$.

Suppose $r\ge1$ and the ground set is a disjoint union of $k$ bases,
so $|S|=kr$. Must there be an ordering $s_1,\ldots,s_{kr}$ of all
elements such that
\[
                    \{s_j,s_{j+1},\ldots,s_{j+r-1}\}
                        \text{ is a basis for every }j,
\]
where subscripts are read modulo $kr$?
The required order is cyclic, including windows that cross its chosen
starting point.

The given basis partition only guarantees independence for $k$ disjoint
blocks. The conclusion requires independence for all overlapping
windows of length $r$. The cyclic order may completely rearrange the
original bases; it need not preserve their internal order or keep them
as consecutive blocks. The question ranges over arbitrary finite
matroids, without assuming a representation over a field. A theorem
for graphic or another representable subclass therefore establishes
only a special case of this universal assertion.

\subsection{Short English statement}
If a matroid's ground set splits into bases, can all its elements
be cyclically arranged so that every rank-sized consecutive block is a basis?
